children: Novo Nordisk A/S (NVO, Financials), the Danish drugmaker best known for its diabetes and obesity treatments, is moving closer to another commercial opportunity outside its biggest franchise.
A European Medicines Agency panel has recommended approval of Frehemgo, Novo's injectable treatment for hemophilia A.
The recommendation covers adults and children, including patients with or without inhibitors.

It follows results from Novo's FRONTIER clinical program. Frehemgo reduced annualized bleeding rates compared with previous clotting-factor preventive treatments and therapies given when bleeding occurred.
The drug could also offer patients more flexibility. Novo plans to sell Frehemgo in a single-use, prefilled pen with dosing options ranging from once weekly to once monthly.
The European Commission still needs to give final approval, but Novo is already preparing for commercialization.
The company expects to introduce Frehemgo in a selected European market during the fourth quarter, followed by a broader European Union rollout early next year.
That timing makes the regulatory decision more than another pipeline update.
Novo remains heavily associated with its blockbuster weight-loss and diabetes drugs. Frehemgo gives investors another business to watch as the company works to broaden its growth base.
The next catalyst is European Commission approval and whether Novo can begin that first launch before year-end.

title: Novo Nordisk's hemophilia drug clears a key hurdle in Europe
